data.narrative:
Medra is a Series A biotech company founded by Michelle Lee that has raised $52M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public comparables in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals, though narrow-filter peer matching proved insufficient for direct median application.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($52M) as a proxy for Series A valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-later-stage progression yields $104M. Public comparables in the sector trade at a median P/S of 5.6x, but this method cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure for the target—standard for private companies. Peer-median triangulation was not viable; while 8 same-sector private companies exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier produced insufficient datapoints for a reliable median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M (low) to $120M (high), centered on $104M. This estimate relies on a single applicable method, creating material uncertainty around the point estimate. Key risks include the stage-progression multiplier's sensitivity to market conditions and Medra's specific commercial readiness relative to peer cohorts. Revenue trajectory and clinical/technical milestones remain critical but unavailable inputs.
